colophon.intro: how this website is actually made.
lines: hand-written html, css and vanilla javascript
zero frameworks — no react, no build step, no npm install
tailwind via cdn for utility classes only
typed.js self-hosted for the terminal tagline
material symbols icon font, subsetted to only the 48 glyphs used (6.7kb)
animation is the web animations api behind a 4kb wrapper — motion.dev's api, not motion.dev's 139kb
guestbook + shoutbox are the comment threads of two public gists — signing is a comment, nothing is committed
hit counter via komarev's ghpvc badge, the same one on my github profile readme
a service worker keeps the whole desktop working offline
jokerz 98 is ~150kb of vanilla js, lazy-loaded only when you open it
its sound effects and music are synthesized in-browser — zero audio files, zero licensing to think about
sir, we have a troll problem reuses the site's own emoji art as monster sprites, no new art needed — each one is composited onto a colour-coded disc so the sprites read as units
become user is a node graph in a json-shaped file — the engine walks it and knows nothing about the story
themes are data, never code — a node registry decides what is customisable and everything else is stripped on load
uploads are scanned by one engine that runs in your browser and again in CI, so a file cannot pass locally and be judged differently on the server
hosted free on github pages, deployed by github actions
audio visualiser + error remix built on the web audio api
every window, game and effect is plain dom + canvas
no trackers. no analytics. no cookie banner. no ads.
installable as an app — there is a web manifest and everything

changes: the repo grid and user.dat used to call the github api anonymously, which is sixty requests an hour per ip — a budget shared by everyone behind one address. so "repos: ?" and "error loading git objects" were what a lot of people actually saw. a workflow now takes a snapshot once a day with a token, writes data/github.json and commits it; the page reads a static file, and it is still there when the connection is not.
the fetcher refuses to write a private repository into that file, and the checks verify the committed one carries none — a snapshot of a public site is not a place to find out afterwards.

the guestbook can be one click now. giscus keeps the same no-backend idea — github holds the words, nothing is committed here — but a visitor signs in and comments instead of copying an entry, opening a gist and pasting it. it is off until two ids are in data/site.json, so the gist board keeps running until then, and a half-filled config falls back rather than showing an empty box.
the frame is on giscus.app so style.css cannot reach into it — giscus-win98.css is passed as its theme instead: same bevels, same greys, same title bars as the window it sits in.

a voyage is a floor you walk now, not a list of buttons. take the boat out and you are put down in a dungeon: rooms on stalks off a spine corridor, welded hatches over the routes you did not take, and the dive lift back to the surface in the entrance room. what stands in a room is what is in it — the creature itself, a burst crate of salvage, a shrine, a bunk. look at it and that is what you get. clear the room and what was standing there becomes the stairs down.

walking the dungeons instead of clicking them turned up a bug that had been in the game since the rebuild: a level-appropriate diver could not win a fight in a trench dungeon. measured, 4% on the first floor and 0% deeper. the spire was 0% everywhere. the room multiplier counted depth twice — the bestiary is already scaled per realm, and it was being multiplied by the realm's layer again on top of that. the balance suite never caught it because it measured bare templates at x1.00, and nothing in the game is ever fought at x1.00.

so the ramp runs from the mouth of a voyage to the bottom of it now, relative to that voyage's own length: every dungeon opens level-appropriate and closes 28% worse. 93/84/93/88% at the mouth, 76/46/53/36% in the deepest room. a second creature in a room ramps 10% to 35% with the descent instead of 35% flat from room one — that flat roll was what actually killed new divers. and no drowned lord waits in room one any more, which was a 20% chance of a death sentence you did not agree to.

the outer three realms have somewhere to go. the echo vault under the reefs, where dredgers file conversations that have not happened yet. the heart room inside the leviathan, where a two-hundred-year-dead heart does eleven beats a minute. the ash chapel above the spire, with a chained penitent who said the beacon was already lit and is waiting to hear whether that was heresy or a report.

crossing between realms is a place instead of a menu. a deep-water hauler is moored one berth along from your own boat on every hub; she lists the realms you have been given the way down to, and takes you. the chart is a reference now — it tells you what is down there and sails you nowhere.
186 headless checks and a browser run that walks a whole voyage: into the room, look at what is in it, fight it, take the stairs, ride the lift back up.

echoes of the tide is 2d now. the menus are gone: you walk. arrow keys or wasd move a diver one tile at a time across hand-drawn maps — vell's landing, the grand anvil, the listening post, the drowned hollow, jawbone station, the last cleat — with a camera that follows and clamps at the edges, and space to look at whatever you are facing.

everything you used to click is a place you stand next to. the boat at the end of the pier takes you on a voyage. the anvil starts the forge. open water opens the fishing spots. a door warps you into the building behind it. a bunk is where you rest until the tide turns.

the people are on the map. harbourmaster vell, a dredger who tells you not to answer anything using your own voice, an ash acolyte who says they are not cruel, only early. the three faction leaders you take the marrow core to — vaelen voss, matriark nahesia, ignis malakor — stand in their own halls, and the act two choice is made by walking up to one of them.

combat is a battle screen. you see your own back on the near platform and the thing you are fighting on the far one, full sprite, on a shadow, with health boxes in the corners the way a handheld would put them. lords get a coat colour derived from their id, so the same lord is the same colour every time you meet it.

an atlas of hand-authored pixel art: the diver in four facings with a walk cycle, nine enemy silhouettes, fifteen tiles, three townsfolk — all palette-indexed, decoded once to offscreen canvases and tinted per draw.
kelp and marrow slicks roll for encounters as you walk over them, with a grace period so you are never jumped twice in three steps.

and the tests walk it: the browser run now steers the diver tile by tile, talks to an npc, takes the boat, fights on the canvas, walks through a door into the anvil hall, forges, comes back out and puts a line in the water. 178 headless checks cover the maps too — every one rectangular, every warp landing somewhere you can stand, every walkable tile reachable from the spawn, and every realm with a boat, an anvil and water within reach.

echoes of the tide, rebuilt to a full six-module design spec. the armour model is now a curve — Armour/(Armour+350), so 350 armour is exactly half mitigation and 1050 is exactly three quarters, and stacking it approaches 100% without ever arriving. nothing in the game, on either side, is untouchable.

a third resource: Marrow. stamina swings the weapon, Marrow casts, sanity is the one the deep attacks. below 25 sanity the interface stops being a reliable narrator and shows you the wrong enemy health and the wrong weaknesses. at zero the Tide picks three turns in ten for you.

hit and dodge are 85% plus the gap between the two, and a miss by up to ten points is a glancing blow: half damage, no crit. you are never quite as safe as the number says and never quite as helpless either.

the nemesis system now starts at the bottom. a nameless Brine Scum that lands the killing blow has a name by morning, a seat among the twelve Deck Captains, and a title taken from how you died — the Carver, the Kindled, the Hollow, the Anvil, the Patient, the Chorus. if all twelve seats are taken it shoulders the weakest one out.

two kills and it looks at the seat above it. promotion takes a Warlord's chair off the incumbent, who is demoted rather than deleted and who remembers it. survive its fire and it grows Pyre-Scarred and may develop a phobia of the stuff. take its eye and attacks from behind land 50% harder for ever after. run, and it learns your knot: +25% to meet your boat.

dungeons are a directed acyclic graph now, not a queue — branching floors, every room reachable from one entrance, a boss at the bottom, and forty generated graphs checked for cycles and orphans on every push.

the forge runs on temperature: hold the metal in the material's real window (300–450 °C for scrap iron, 1400 and up for a celestial core), then three hammer strikes at a moving sweet spot. score out of 100 into four bands — Defective, Standard, Masterwork, and Abyssal-Forged, which comes off the anvil humming.

six rarity tiers with prefix and suffix naming, so you carry a Brine-Hardened Chitin Harpoon of the Mind-Eater rather than a Rare Harpoon. Cursed gear is deliberately the strongest thing you can hold: Leaking Seals is +50% physical damage for four sanity every turn of every fight.

angling is a tension sim with a green band at 40–80 — the only place the fish's stamina goes down — and a surge that arrives as a jerk rather than a ramp, which is the entire reason a heavier rod is worth carrying. hold on to a trench fish with hemp tackle and you lose the line.

saves have a DJB2 checksum, a backup slot written from the previous good save rather than the current one, base64 export/import of a whole run, and a migration loop that walks an old save forward one version at a time and refuses one from the future.

the design document is in the repo at games/ECHOES-GDD.md and 155 automated checks hold the code to it — the armour curve, the published XP table to the digit, the nine named skills with their exact costs, Morvath's three phases mechanic for mechanic, the seat counts, and a few thousand simulated fights. where the spec and a playable game could not both be had, the doc says so and shows the measurement.

echoes of the tide: leviathan's wake — a grimdark RPG in a win98 window. three hundred years ago the celestial sun came out of the sky and went into the trench, the sea rose to meet the hole it left, and it has never gone back down. forty thousand people are still floating on what is left, and this morning a line came up with a piece of worked brass on it, and the brass was warm.

the drowned lords remember you. seventeen of them — twelve captains, four warlords and whatever is at the bottom of the spire — grown from your seed and kept for the whole run. kill you and one takes a title from the way you died (the carver, the kindled, the hollow, the anvil, the patient, the chorus), twenty percent more hit points and an armour upgrade. run from one and it learns your knot and starts meeting your boat. survive enough fire and it grows a scar that makes it immune to fire and softer to everything else — every mutation writes a matching weakness, so a heavily scarred lord is more answerable, not just harder.

beat a captain three times and it takes a warlord's seat off the incumbent, who is demoted rather than removed, and who remembers that. a kill only sticks if it was permanent — an inquisitor pyre, a dredger unmaking, or a leviathan-bone edge through the neck. anything else comes back a rank down, poorly drowned and much angrier.
five attributes, fifty levels, three skill trees of eight nodes — marrow-smith, tide-weaver, harpooner — and only fifty points for a hundred and twenty ranks, so you cannot have all of it.

sanity is a second health bar that only the deep attacks. below seventy percent you hear things, below forty you see things that are not in this realm, below fifteen the tide talks to you directly and everything costs an extra stamina. at zero you are not lost — you are recruited, and your character joins the roster of the next run on that seed, wearing what you were wearing.

deep-forge smithing across five material tiers behind a heat-and-quench minigame: hold the metal in a band that narrows with tier and widens with your marrow-smith rank, then three hammer strikes at a moving sweet spot. get it wrong and you get a cursed piece, which is one affix at masterwork strength plus one curse, and which the dredgers consider correct. sockets take runes, and two runes in one item are worth more than one each in two — the syndicate calls it resonance and charges for it.

dredging is a line-tension simulation integrated at 60hz. hold to reel, release to give slack, and watch depth and tension fight each other while the thing on the end of it thrashes. a deep fish at high tide on a tier-one line is a snapped line; that is the lesson. the eldritch band is not a catch at all — it is something that was fishing back.

a tide clock of eight ticks a day drives all of it. night brings nightmares and rare fish, high tide floods the trench nodes for an extra danger and an extra loot tier, low tide opens wrecks that are otherwise underwater, and at witching plus high tide the leviathan turns over and every lord in the realm is awake at once.

four realms behind a pressure gate, node-based dungeons dealt from a deck that gets meaner with depth, four multi-phase bosses with environmental triggers — the rust mother floods the deck and puts out every fire, the leviathan rolls twice and tears your gear off, the beacon's heart is finished at 1 hp against four rounds of air — branching dialogue with skill checks derived from your attributes, an eighteen-entry codex, and four endings, none of them clean.

specified before it was built: games/ECHOES-GDD.md is the design document and 120 automated checks hold the source to it — the crit table, the xp curve, the nemesis limits, the save round trip through key-shortening, and a few thousand simulated fights that fail the build if the balance drifts. a browser run rolls a character, sails, fights, forges and puts a line in the water on every push.

defrag.exe grew a real disk under it. the clusters are the files this page actually downloaded, at the sizes they actually weigh — the browser keeps that list, so nothing had to be invented and nothing can be wrong about it. hover a cluster and it tells you whose it is.

it defragments for real too: the scaffolding of the site sits in a system area at the front and never moves, everything else gets pulled forward into one piece each, and the free space ends up as a single lump at the bottom
a file that would leave a big gap in front of a bad cluster gets written straight across it instead, because skipping forty percent of a drive to avoid one split is vandalism rather than tidying
speed control, pause, stop, and the dialog at the end that tells you it did not make anything faster
57 checks on the plan — the one that matters replays every move and counts the clusters, because the first version lost some and looked perfectly fine doing it

every ante in jokerz 98 has a face now, and they are the cursed pack — ante 1 could not care less, ante 8 wants you dead. the small and big blind of an ante are the same opponent at a different hue, and the boss is somebody else entirely, keeping its own face wherever it turns up.
beat a blind and a yellow head drops out of the top of the window, lands on theirs with a BONK, bounces once and falls out of the bottom

fixed: the chips and mult readout kept showing the previous hand after you played one, which looked exactly like the game had failed to recalculate. it reads zero when nothing is selected — the last hand is still reported on its own line underneath.
fixed: starting a run floated a cheerful "$NaN" over the money counter, because the menu screen has no money to compare against yet

jokerz 98 moves now. the real fix underneath: the table was rebuilt with innerHTML on every click, so the card you selected was destroyed and recreated already raised — the transition it had all along never got to play. selecting a card now touches that card and the readout, nothing else.
so picking a card lifts with a little overshoot, hovering raises it, and a full hand nudges instead of going quiet
discarded cards fly to the deck one after another before they leave your hand, and whatever replaces them is dealt back in
the blind takes the hit visibly: the bar shudders, the fill runs up, the total floats off it as damage, and the score counts up instead of snapping
jokers jump when they fire and say what they did, every button acknowledges the click, money that changes says so, and a new screen arrives rather than appearing
all of it through fx.js, so unticking window animations turns off every bit of it — css transitions included — and the game plays exactly the same

windows, menus and toasts move now — a motion layer (fx.js) built on the web animations api, with the api shape borrowed from motion.dev and springs sampled into a linear() easing curve the same way it does
borrowed the shape rather than the bundle on purpose: motion.dev's vanilla build is 139kb, this is about four, and the site still has no build step and no dependencies

the reduced-motion setting is finally honoured — the os one, plus a new "window animations" tickbox in display properties. off means nothing animates and the end state lands instantly, cursor sparkles included

task manager's performance tab is no longer decorative text: live cpu and memory history, a load ring and per-process bars, drawn on canvas in perfmon green (charts.js, composable pieces borrowed from bklit ui)
57 checks on the lot, including the one that matters — ask for less motion and nothing moves
wizardz reads your drawing better — the tilt search reaches ±30° instead of ±18°, so a sigil drawn at a real-world lean stops falling off the end of it (89% of them cast now, up from 67%)
and it is twice as fast doing it: the ink grid picks which lean each spell is judged at, so thirty point-cloud matches run instead of five hundred and fifty

the score now charges you for wandering — how much line you used and how much your hand turned, both measured against the sigil you were aiming for, so a doodle that crosses the right area no longer scores like a spell
casting bar lowered to 60%: a drawing only has to be recognisably the thing, and power is measured from there up — scrape in and the spell is weak, draw it clean and it hits full
fizzles say which failure it was: "half fireball, half frostbolt" is a different problem from "too rough", and the practice pad now shows the bar and the power
the guestbook is a github gist now, and signing it is a comment on that gist — hit sign it, your entry is copied, the gist opens, you paste it. same for the shoutbox.
so no more pull request (which quietly meant forking the whole repo to say hello), no issue, no robot with write access committing a stranger's text
the site reads the comment thread straight off the public gist api, so an entry shows up without waiting for a deploy — the old json entries are still on the wall
the github account that wrote it is shown next to whatever name was typed, and every entry is escaped where it is rendered
moderating is deleting the comment
multiplayer — lobbies with five letter invite codes, an invite link, chat and a ready check, running peer to peer over webrtc so it works straight off github pages with no server
wizardz 98 — a 1v1 wizard duel where the only way to cast anything is to draw its sigil on the arena
50 spells across 10 elements, each with its own sigil, checked in CI so no two of them look alike to the recogniser
customisable wizards: hats, beards, robes, staffs, familiars, auras and titles, all drawn in code and carried into the duel with you
a grimoire with every sigil, a practice pad that scores your drawing, and an eight slot quick reference strip
the recogniser allows for a tilted hand: a sigil drawn at a twenty degree lean used to be a coin flip and now lands 100 times out of 100, while a panic scribble still casts nothing

1 v bot — six named opponents with their own spell tastes and hands: bogwart throws whatever he can spell, old gary hides behind a wall, nyx makes everything stick, and the tax collector takes your mana first
each bot runs the same simulation a human opponent does, on three difficulties, and has opinions about how the round went
the netplay layer is generic — future games register themselves and get the lobby for free

a second way online that is not p2p at all: the duel is posted through public nostr relays on port 443, encrypted with the invite code, for the school and office networks that block webrtc — still no server and no signup
an optional self-hosted websocket relay as the third option (server/relay.js, no dependencies)
every window has a fullscreen button now — canvas games scale up to fill the screen and keep their aspect ratio
become user — an original branching interactive drama in nine chapters, about three programs on a 1999 home PC noticing they are running
timed choices, quick-time events, scene inspection, and a per-chapter flowchart showing what you took and what you never found
eight endings decided by what you actually did, chapter select, and full local save
theme maker — customise 29 named parts of the desktop, one property at a time, with the whole site repainting as you type
themes can carry scheduled events: fire on a clock, an interval, a date, a weekday, an idle timer, or only inside a time window
themes can bring a song, which joins the winamp playlist while the theme is on
publish sends a theme off as a pull request, the same way the guestbook works — merged ones show up in everyone's gallery
every uploaded file is scanned in the browser and again in CI, with a virustotal reputation lookup on the server side
5 built-in presets to start from, plus a one-click generator that builds a whole palette from a single colour
troll problem rebuilt as an actual tower defense — the first version was a horde-survival game wearing the name
5 maps with fixed troll routes, 10 towers with 3 upgrade tiers each, per-tower targeting priority and a sell button
30 hand-authored waves, 9 troll types with armour, flight, healing, shields and summons, bosses at 10/20/25/30
an 8-node crystal upgrade tree that persists between runs, plus a wave telegraph, early-call bonus and 1x/2x/3x speed
sir, we have a troll problem — an original mini-game using the site's own emoji art as monster sprites
full local save: mid-run resume plus permanent progression that never resets
synthesized sound, no audio files, lazy-loaded so the desktop stays fast
hit counter now actually counts site visits — swapped the github-profile-coupled badge for a real per-page counter
no signup, no key, verified to increment on every request before shipping
jokerz 98 now has sound — every effect is synthesized live with the Web Audio API, no audio files
a scoring animation: cards flash, jokers pulse when they trigger, chips and mult tally up live
a small original background loop, toggleable with the music button in the game window
jokerz 98 — a full poker roguelike, built into the desktop
165 jokers, 22 tarots, 12 planets, 21 spectrals, 35 vouchers
31 boss blinds, 17 decks, 8 stakes, 15 booster packs, 20 skip tags
seeded runs, saved runs, and 15 jokers that exist nowhere else
klondike solitaire with undo, auto-finish and the win cascade
five screensavers — mystify, starfield, 3d pipes, flying windows, bouncing logo
defrag.exe, the most hypnotic program microsoft ever shipped
a devlog, and a find: files search across everything on the site
works offline now, plus a real 404, humans.txt, robots.txt and sitemap
added /now, /uses, /colophon and changelog pages
88x31 button wall + link-to-me badge
shrine, internet history timeline and site map
'which track are you' personality quiz
rss feed and status widget in the tray
minesweeper, snake, pong, paint, notepad, calculator, terminal
my computer, recycle bin, control panel, dial-up simulator
23 achievements, 12 screen effects, magic 8-ball and toys
start menu flyouts, right-click desktop menu, calendar popup
windows error remix when you end every process
live repo demos in fake internet explorer windows
guestbook + shoutbox moved to github pull requests
self-hosted icon font, fixed all the broken glyphs
windows 98 taskbar, start menu and boot screen
winamp player with visualiser and per-track themes
canvas matrix rain, konami code, troll invasion
the shithole opens its doors

boards.note: each board is a public gist, and its comment thread is the board. paste the gist id (the hex blob in its url) here — see data/README.md.
